subject: Parsing error when incorporating Bayesian P-value GOF test, MSOM

messages.author: 62dd58f80f03b3d8
messages.subject: Parsing error when incorporating Bayesian P-value GOF test, MSOM
parts:
Hi all,

I have a MSOM and iI am trying to incorporate code to calculate a Bayesian p-value as a goodness of fit test into my existing MSOM code in JAGS. The original code/model ran fine, but I am getting a syntax/parsing error when trying to incorporate code to calculate the Bayesian P-value. Specifically the error is: "Error parsing model file: syntax error on line 15 near "," ". In R, this is line: "mu.p[i, k] <- (p[i, k] * z[i, k], nOcc[i])". It would seem to me like it's having an error with the comma before n0cc[i] (which incorporates differences in the number of survey replicates per site) but the model runs fine when the code to calculate the p-value is not incorporated, so I'm a little stumped. I'm following along with code from Bajaru et al. 2019 which uses chi2 disrepancies. It is similar to code from Tobler et al. 2015  which uses Pearson residuals.

Any insight on what might be happening would be appreciated! I'll include my original code (which runs) below, and the updated code with the new sections to calculate the Bayesian P-value below it. 

Original code:

model{
  for(k in 1:M){  # Loop through species
    w[k] ~ dbern(omega)

    # Likelihood
    for(i in 1:nSites) {
       # Ecological model
      logit(psi[i, k]) <- b0[k] + bFor[k] * forest[i] +
          bFor2[k] * forest2[i]
       z[i, k] ~ dbern(psi[i, k] * w[k])
       # Observation model
       logit(p[i, k]) <- a0[k] + aTrail[k] * trail[i]
       y[i, k] ~ dbin(p[i, k] * z[i, k], nOcc[i])
    }

    # Priors (species level)/species heterogeneity
    b0[k] ~ dnorm(mu.b0, tau.b0)
    mu.eta[k] <- mu.a0 + rho * sd.a0/sd.b0 *
        (b0[k] - mu.b0)
    a0[k] ~ dnorm(mu.eta[k], tau.eta)

    bFor[k] ~ dnorm(mu.bforest, tau.bforest)
    bFor2[k] ~ dnorm(mu.bforest2, tau.bforest2)

    aTrail[k]~ dnorm(mu.atrail, tau.atrail)
  }

  # Hyperpriors (community level)
  omega ~ dbeta(0.001, 1) #Link's scale prior
   

## for occupancy
  mu.b0 ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.b0 ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.b0 <- 1/sd.b0^2

  mu.bforest ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.bforest ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.bforest <- 1/sd.bforest^2
  mu.bforest2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.bforest2 ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.bforest2 <- 1/sd.bforest2^2
 
##for detection
  mu.a0 ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.a0 ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.a0 <- 1/sd.a0^2

  mu.atrail ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.atrail ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)  
  tau.atrail <- 1/sd.atrail^2

  rho ~ dunif(-1, 1)
  tau.eta <- tau.a0/(1 - rho^2)

  # Derived quantities
  for(i in 1:nSites) {
  Nsite[i] <- sum(z[i,]) #richness per site
  }
  N <- sum(w)                 # Total metacommunity size
 
}

Code with GOF test:

model{
  for(k in 1:M){  # Loop through species
    w[k] ~ dbern(omega)

    # Likelihood
    for(i in 1:nSites) {
       # Ecological model
      logit(psi[i, k]) <- b0[k] + bFor[k] * forest[i] +
          bFor2[k] * forest2[i]
       z[i, k] ~ dbern(psi[i, k] * w[k])
       # Observation model
       logit(p[i, k]) <- a0[k] + aTrail[k] * trail[i]
       mu.p[i, k] <- (p[i, k] * z[i, k], nOcc[i])
       y[i, k] ~ dbin(mu.p[i, k])

##Goodness of fit tests

#create simulated dataset to calculate Bayesian p-value
ynew.sim[i, k] ~ dbin(mu.p[i, k])
e.count[i, k] <- mu.p[i, k] #expected datum

# Chi-square discrepancy for the actual data
chi2.actual[i, k] <- pow((y[i, k] - e.count[i, k]),2) / (e.count[i, k] + e) # Add small value e to denominator to avoid division by zero

#Chi-square discrepancy for the simulated ('perfect') data
chi2.sim[i, k] <- pow((ynew.sim[i, k] - e.count[i, k]),2) / (e.count[i, k] + e)

    }

    # Priors (species level)/species heterogeneity
    b0[k] ~ dnorm(mu.b0, tau.b0)
    mu.eta[k] <- mu.a0 + rho * sd.a0/sd.b0 *
        (b0[k] - mu.b0)
    a0[k] ~ dnorm(mu.eta[k], tau.eta)

    bFor[k] ~ dnorm(mu.bforest, tau.bforest)
    bFor2[k] ~ dnorm(mu.bforest2, tau.bforest2)

    aTrail[k]~ dnorm(mu.atrail, tau.atrail)
  }

  # Hyperpriors (community level)
  omega ~ dbeta(0.001, 1) #Link's scale prior
   

## for occupancy
  mu.b0 ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.b0 ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.b0 <- 1/sd.b0^2

  mu.bforest ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.bforest ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.bforest <- 1/sd.bforest^2
  mu.bforest2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.bforest2 ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.bforest2 <- 1/sd.bforest2^2
 
##for detection
  mu.a0 ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.a0 ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.a0 <- 1/sd.a0^2

  mu.atrail ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.atrail ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)  
  tau.atrail <- 1/sd.atrail^2

  rho ~ dunif(-1, 1)
  tau.eta <- tau.a0/(1 - rho^2)

  # Derived quantities

  for(i in 1:nSites) {
  Nsite[i] <- sum(z[i,]) #richness per site
  }
  N <- sum(w)                 # Total metacommunity size

 # Add up individual chi2 values for overall fit statistic
    fit.actual <- sum(chi2.actual[,,]) # Fit statistic for actual data set
    fit.sim <- sum(chi2.sim[,,])       # Fit statistic for a fitting model
    bpv <- step(fit.sim-fit.actual)    # Bayesian p-value
 
}


Thank you!

Jordan

messages.subject: AW: Parsing error when incorporating Bayesian P-value GOF test, MSOM
parts:
The critical line must either be stochastic as
mu.p[i, k] ~ dbin(p[i, k] * z[i, k], nOcc[i])
or deterministic as
mu.p[i, k] <- p[i, k] * z[i, k] * nOcc[i]
but not a mix between the two.

Kind regards

Michael

You might want to check out Conn et al. (2018). I've stopped bothering with GOF tests for occupancy models in light of what they say. It doesn't seem like GOF tests are particularly useful for binary data.

Conn, P.B., Johnson, D.S., Williams, P.J., Melin, S.R. & Hooten, M.B. (2018) A guide to Bayesian model checking for ecologists. Ecological Monographs, 88, 526-542.

Betreff: Parsing error when incorporating Bayesian P-value GOF test, MSOM
 
Hi all,

I have a MSOM and iI am trying to incorporate code to calculate a Bayesian p-value as a goodness of fit test into my existing MSOM code in JAGS. The original code/model ran fine, but I am getting a syntax/parsing error when trying to incorporate code to calculate the Bayesian P-value. Specifically the error is: "Error parsing model file: syntax error on line 15 near "," ". In R, this is line: "mu.p[i, k] <- (p[i, k] * z[i, k], nOcc[i])". It would seem to me like it's having an error with the comma before n0cc[i] (which incorporates differences in the number of survey replicates per site) but the model runs fine when the code to calculate the p-value is not incorporated, so I'm a little stumped. I'm following along with code from Bajaru et al. 2019 which uses chi2 disrepancies. It is similar to code from Tobler et al. 2015  which uses Pearson residuals.

Any insight on what might be happening would be appreciated! I'll include my original code (which runs) below, and the updated code with the new sections to calculate the Bayesian P-value below it. 

Original code:

model{
  for(k in 1:M){  # Loop through species
    w[k] ~ dbern(omega)

    # Likelihood
    for(i in 1:nSites) {
       # Ecological model
      logit(psi[i, k]) <- b0[k] + bFor[k] * forest[i] +
          bFor2[k] * forest2[i]
       z[i, k] ~ dbern(psi[i, k] * w[k])
       # Observation model
       logit(p[i, k]) <- a0[k] + aTrail[k] * trail[i]
       y[i, k] ~ dbin(p[i, k] * z[i, k], nOcc[i])
    }

    # Priors (species level)/species heterogeneity
    b0[k] ~ dnorm(mu.b0, tau.b0)
    mu.eta[k] <- mu.a0 + rho * sd.a0/sd.b0 *
        (b0[k] - mu.b0)
    a0[k] ~ dnorm(mu.eta[k], tau.eta)

    bFor[k] ~ dnorm(mu.bforest, tau.bforest)
    bFor2[k] ~ dnorm(mu.bforest2, tau.bforest2)

    aTrail[k]~ dnorm(mu.atrail, tau.atrail)
  }

  # Hyperpriors (community level)
  omega ~ dbeta(0.001, 1) #Link's scale prior
   

## for occupancy
  mu.b0 ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.b0 ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.b0 <- 1/sd.b0^2

  mu.bforest ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.bforest ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.bforest <- 1/sd.bforest^2
  mu.bforest2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.bforest2 ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.bforest2 <- 1/sd.bforest2^2
 
##for detection
  mu.a0 ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.a0 ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)
  tau.a0 <- 1/sd.a0^2

  mu.atrail ~ dnorm(0, 0.2)
  sd.atrail ~ dt(0, 1, 1)T(0,)  
  tau.atrail <- 1/sd.atrail^2

  rho ~ dunif(-1, 1)
  tau.eta <- tau.a0/(1 - rho^2)

  # Derived quantities
  for(i in 1:nSites) {
  Nsite[i] <- sum(z[i,]) #richness per site
  }
  N <- sum(w)                 # Total metacommunity size
 
}
